title: qe-dv stacked-bar
description: Root node emitted by the datavis `stacked-bar` directive at contract 1.0: one or more proportional stacked bars sharing a single ordered set of categories. The node is a portable MyST `div`; the measured data rides as properties and the children are a genuine table carrying the same measured numbers, so a theme with no custom renderer still shows every value. The data lives exactly twice — once in the properties, once rendered in the fallback — and no node the directive emits carries a top-level `label`, `identifier` or `html_id`, because `myst-cli`'s embed transform deletes all three from any node that is not a crossReference, cite, footnote, captionNumber or link.

type.description: Always the portable `div` node type. The contract defines no custom node types, because `myst-to-tex` silently drops a subtree whose node type it has no handler for.

class.description: The two canonical tokens in this order, then any author tokens from the directive's `:class:` option. The directive normalises: it splits `:class:` on whitespace, drops empty and duplicate tokens, and joins with single spaces.

contract.description: Version of the datavis node contract this node conforms to. A consumer that does not recognise the version renders the children instead. Only the root carries it; no node inside the fallback does.

primitive.description: Primitive name, for consumers that dispatch on a property rather than on a class selector. Only the root carries it; no node inside the fallback does.

dimension.description: Name of the categorical dimension the bars are broken into, from the directive argument. Heads the first column of the fallback table and is the figure's natural accessible name.

unit.description: What the segment values count, in lower case. Always present in the fallback's corner header cell as `dimension (unit)`.

labels.description: Inline segment label style for a drawing consumer: "full" renders category and value together (HIGH · 20), "value" renders the value alone (20).

legend.description: Whether a drawing consumer should place a category colour key beneath the bars. The fallback table needs none: it names every category down its first column, under a corner cell naming the dimension.

size.description: Role hint, not a pixel height: "md" is a headline bar standing on its own, "sm" is one row in a stack of comparable bars.

categories.description: The stack order, shared by every bar and never re-ordered by a consumer. With a body table it comes from the header row, left to right; with `:file:` from `:categories:`.

bars.description: One entry per bar, in author order — one body row of the authored table, or one selected row of the CSV. Consumers never sort.

children.description: The portable fallback: exactly one child, the table carrying every measured number the props carry — every category label, every bar label, every segment value and every bar total. `share` is the one number it omits, being exactly reconstructible from `value` and `total`. One child and one shape is what lets a consumer or a test read the fallback without branching on `bars.length`.

prefixItems.title: fallback table
prefixItems.description: Row 0 is the one header row, naming the dimension, the unit and every bar; every following row is a body row — one per category, then a bold Total row.

children.description: At least a header row, one category row and the Total row. Every row is either the header row — every cell a header — or a body row, in which no cell is a header, and the table holds exactly one of the former. Two things this cannot say, both asserted by the plugin's tests instead: that the header row is row 0 (JSON Schema pins a position only inside a closed tuple, and the row count is open), and that every row carries the same number of cells, `1 + bars.length`, since no keyword compares one array's length with another's.

inlineNode.description: The permitted inline subset inside a fallback cell — the family's allowed node types, narrowed to the ones that can appear inline. `myst-to-tex` has no handler for `grid`, `card` or a custom node type and drops the whole subtree silently while the build still exits 0, so the cell's content is held to types every export path handles.

headerRow.title: header row
headerRow.description: Row 0, and the only row in the table whose cells are headers. `myst-to-tex` writes an `\hline` after every row whose first cell is a header, and its long-table path counts leading header rows to find where the body starts — so a header cell in a later row rules the table after every line, and in the long-table path makes the header count equal the row count and the body loop skip every row.

children.description: The corner cell, then one cell per bar in `bars` order.

bodyRow.title: body row
bodyRow.description: One category row, or the final Total row. No cell in it is a header.

children.description: The row-label cell, then one value cell per bar in `bars` order — the same count as the header row's.

headerCell.title: header cell
headerCell.description: One cell of row 0. Structure only: a cell carries no `contract`, no `primitive` and no copy of the datum it renders.

header.description: True on every cell of row 0, and on no cell anywhere else.

bodyCell.title: body cell
bodyCell.description: One cell of a row after row 0. Structure only: a cell carries no `contract`, no `primitive` and no copy of the datum it renders.

header.description: Never true outside row 0. The directive omits the property altogether on a body cell; `false` is tolerated so a tree round-tripped through a serialiser that fills defaults still validates.

category.title: category
category.description: One step of the stack, shared by every bar.

label.description: Display text for the category and simultaneously its key: `bars[].segments[i].category` equals this string. In a body table it is the header cell's text; with `:file:` it is also the CSV column header the values were read from.

tone.description: Closed-vocabulary colour hint, never a colour and never a threshold. Repeats are legal; a consumer must still render two adjacent same-tone segments distinguishably.

bar.title: bar
bar.description: One bar: a labelled composition over the shared categories.

label.description: Row label for this bar, and this bar's column header in the fallback table. Required on every bar, including a lone one, so that the fallback has one shape.

total.description: Sum of this bar's segment values, denormalised so that no consumer has to reduce and the fallback's Total row cannot disagree with the drawn bar.

segments.description: Exactly parallel to `categories`: same length, same order, zero-valued entries included.

segment.title: segment
segment.description: One category's contribution to one bar.

category.description: Equal to `categories[i].label` at the same index. Redundant with the index, kept so a segment is self-describing when logged on its own.

value.description: The measured quantity for this category in this bar. Not necessarily an integer; never negative and never a silent zero standing in for missing data. A composition has no absent state, so `value` is never null and the family's em-dash rendering of an absent value never appears in this fallback: a source cell holding one of the family's null tokens is an error, not a null.

share.description: The number nearest `value / total * 100` at one decimal place, so every renderer sizes segments identically; 0 when `total` is 0.
